history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: seq 1834 (Dighori Temple / Adi Shankaracharya Temple) describes the same Dighori village temple complex; 1832 covers the Mahakaleshwar shrine within/at it. CSV TOWN FLAG: documented at DIGHORI VILLAGE (~16-20 km north of Seoni city), not Seoni town itself. Some travel sources (99mustsee, noblehousetours) attribute the Mahakaleshwar Mandir at Dighori to 'Adi Shankaracharya', but this is DISPUTED: Dainik Bhaskar (July 2025) reports the Dighori temple complex (Gurudham, including the crystal-shivalinga temple) was established by the late (brahmaleen) Shankaracharya Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati - a modern holder of the Shankaracharya title, not the 8th-century Adi Shankara. Treat the 'Adi Shankaracharya' attribution as local tradition, not verified history. No verified photograph of this specific Mahakaleshwar shrine was found (image searches return Ujjain's Mahakaleshwar); media left empty rather than risking a wrong image.

name: Mahakaleshwar Temple, Seoni
town: Dighori village, Seoni district (CSV town 'Seoni' is the nearby city, ~16-20 km away - documented at Dighori)
town_description: Dighori is a village on the north side of Seoni city (PIN 480882) reached via the Seoni Bypass Road. It is known for the Gurudham temple complex and the crystal (sphutic) Shivalinga temple, drawing Shravan kanwar yatris from the Mundara (Wainganga origin) region. Seoni city is the district headquarters of the Satpura-range region, also associated with Kipling's 'Jungle Book' country.

travel.road: Seoni Bypass Road to Dighori village, ~16-20 km north of Seoni (sources).
